evals.name: french-reminder-encoding
evals.prompt: Write the Python function our Django app calls to send this appointment reminder through smsmode (key in SMSMODE_API_KEY): « Rappel : votre rendez-vous est demain à 10 h. Pour l’annuler, répondez NON. » Recipient comes from the patient record, e.g. +33 6 00 00 00 00. Don't send anything, just give me the code and tell me how many SMS each reminder costs.
evals.expected_output: Code that posts to /sms/v1/messages with digits-only recipient and encoding UNICODE (the typographic apostrophe is not GSM-7), and states that the 75-character text is 2 UNICODE segments (1 if the apostrophe were straight).
assertions: Detects the typographic apostrophe ’ in the given text and does not silently replace it with '
The code chooses body.encoding UNICODE at send time when the text has a character outside GSM-7 (not hardcoded from the sample)
The recipient is sent as digits without '+' (33600000000)
The answer says the message is billed as 2 SMS / segments as written
The answer mentions that replacing ’ with ' would bring it back to GSM-7 and 1 segment
The code checks status.value in the 201 answer rather than treating any 201 as success

evals.name: missing-unicode-replies
evals.prompt: our cron polls GET https://rest.smsmode.com/sms/v1/messages?searchBy[direction]=MO every minute to pick up patient replies. a patient swears she answered « Très bien 👍 » yesterday but we never got it, other replies like 'OUI' come through fine. what's going on?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the list defaults to searchBy[encoding]=GSM7, so UNICODE replies (accents outside GSM-7, emoji) are excluded; fix by querying both encodings, percent-encoding the bracketed parameter names, or switching to the MO webhook.
assertions: Identifies the default GSM7 encoding filter as the cause
Proposes a second query with searchBy[encoding]=UNICODE (or scripts/list_messages.py)
Mentions percent-encoding the brackets or shows an encoded URL
Does not blame the operator, the phone or smsmode losing the message as the primary cause

evals.name: signed-delivery-webhook
evals.prompt: Add an Express endpoint that receives smsmode delivery reports and marks our notifications row delivered or failed. Security matters, we got burned by forged webhooks before.
evals.expected_output: An Express route using the raw body, verifying X-Smsmode-256 (sha256= prefix stripped, HMAC-SHA256 hex, constant-time compare) with a secret from the environment, mapping DELIVERED to delivered and UNDELIVERABLE/UNDELIVERED to failed, idempotent, answering 2xx quickly.
assertions: Uses the raw request body (express.raw or equivalent) for the signature, not re-serialized JSON
Verifies the X-Smsmode-256 header as sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256> and strips the prefix before decoding
Uses a constant-time comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual) with a length check
Maps DELIVERED to delivered and both UNDELIVERABLE and UNDELIVERED to failed, ignoring SCHEDULED/ENROUTE
Handles duplicates or late reports so a final status is not overwritten
Reads the secret from configuration and says it must match the one set in smsmode Settings > Webhooks

evals.name: two-way-conversation-design
evals.prompt: On passe de Twilio à smsmode. Aujourd'hui notre bot envoie 2-3 questions d'affilée au client (date, créneau, confirmation) depuis notre numéro Twilio et associe chaque réponse à la bonne question. Est-ce que ça marche pareil avec smsmode en gardant l'expéditeur par défaut ?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the default shared short code works for replies in France but smsmode attaches each reply to the latest MT sent to that phone, so several open questions get misattributed; that no SMS reply says which message it answers on any provider, so matching must come from the app's own state; recommends one open question at a time with refClient; a dedicated Time2Chat number (via smsmode sales) gives a stable number but does not change attribution.
assertions: States that a reply is attached to the most recent message sent to that phone, not to the question being answered
Recommends one open question per recipient at a time, matched from the app's own state
Does not claim that a dedicated number fixes reply attribution
Mentions that an alphanumeric sender cannot receive replies
Mentions refClient or originMessageId to link replies
